text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--- Denmark's centre-left minority government is poised for two long days of political combat with the opposition Liberals and Conservatives in parliament on next year's state budget due to be passed before the Christmas recess at the end of the week. Despite the fact that general elections are not due in Denmark until autumn 1998, the budget debate is seen by some analysts as the start of the election campaign.
--- The growing number of telephone and personal computer banks means that banks will have to inform private clients better, which could affect their earnings in the future, top bankers foresee.

--- Homogenous Denmark could become split down the middle into groups of well-educated employees on the one side and unskilled labourers on the other if the state does not spend more on educating Danes with low educational levels, a report states.
--- Danish research companies are moving more of their activities abroad with top executives of Denmark's 100 largest research companies seeing this as the only way to survive, a new survey shows.
--- Danish telecommmunications group Tele Danmark is negotiating with French media group Canal Plus on television cooperation with its Danish Multichoice unit.
